title: The FSD reads the ACE views and the batch-status view directly, while Architecture v5 gives that read to rwb-source-data alone and the connection matrix gives S8 only an R and an E to P1
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 12, 13 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-05 and DP-13
section: A1.1 constraints; A2.1.3.1 to A2.19.3.1 validation rules VR-S8-001-1 to VR-S8-019-1; A2.1.2, A2.13.2, A2.14.2, A2.15.2 and A2.16.2 integration points
description: The FSD states that source data is read only from the ACE database through the SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, landed by ACE's own ingestion with no inbound load in the Workbench, and nine of the nineteen features carry validation rule VR-S8-00n-1 against v_ace_batch_status. Architecture v5 slide 45 answers 'who reads ACE data' with rwb-source-data alone and gives everyone else REST or a Temporal activity, slide 12 repeats that only rwb-source-data reads the SQL views, and the slide 13 connection matrix gives the S8 row one R and one E to P1 and no other data cell at all. The read path the FSD describes therefore cannot be built as written.
evidence: FSD S8 A1.1 Constraints; VR-S8-001-1, VR-S8-002-1, VR-S8-003-1, VR-S8-004-1, VR-S8-005-1, VR-S8-006-1, VR-S8-007-1, VR-S8-009-1 and VR-S8-015-1. Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views), slide 12 (need ACE data: ask rwb-source-data), slide 13 (S8 row: R E to P1, E to P3, T E to P10, no other cell).
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-062, RWB-E2-015, RWB-E2-029, RWB-E7-001 to RWB-E7-010
proposed: Carry the FSD's field names as the source field names that the rwb-source-data contract returns, and build every step on that contract with the boundary test failing the build on a view read or an ACE table read. Confirm the party-flag, deceased-marker and freshness fields with P1 before the wave 2 system test.

title: Three FSD integration points name the Quartz scheduler, which Architecture v5 and the Temporal design replace with durable timers in DeviationWorkflow
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 25 and 31; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 24; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-10 and R6
section: A2.2.2, A2.3.2 and A2.6.2 integration points; A2.2.3.1 R-DEV-01 and R-DEV-18; A2.3.3.1 R-DEV-08
description: The pause, the prescription clock and the resume each name 'Workbench, Quartz scheduler' as their integration point, and the FSD's own rules R-DEV-01, R-DEV-08 and R-DEV-18 describe the pause and the resume as state moves. Architecture v5 slide 25 makes each stage a Temporal child workflow, slide 31 states that the ACE shared Quartz tables are no longer used, and DP-10 replaces every Quartz job with a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow. The service keeps the behaviour and none of the scheduler dependency.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.2.2, A2.3.2, A2.6.2 ('Integration points. Workbench, Quartz scheduler'). Architecture v5 slide 25 (a child workflow per stage, DeviationWorkflow on rwb-deviation) and slide 31 (Quartz tables no longer used). Temporal and Drools Design slide 8 ('the deviation is a signal; the workflow pauses its stage timer but not the prescription timer') and slide 24 step 2. Rules DP-10 and R6 (TE-007 retired).
proposed: State the pause, the prescription clock and the resume as durable timers inside DeviationWorkflow through the workflow kit, and drop the Quartz row from the integration list of this service. No Quartz table, connection or job is named as a dependency of S8.

title: The deviation REST operations disagree between the Architecture slide, the Ownership Map and the FSD, and no read operation is recorded for the case record deviation query that the FSD times at two seconds
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 and slide 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints; Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.2.4.3 and A2.7.4.2
section: A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-S8-002-02 (deviation query does not answer within 2 seconds); A2.7.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-007-02 (GET /cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs); A2.1 to A2.19 (raise, clear and read)
description: Architecture v5 slide 15 gives the service GET and POST /deviations and POST /deviations/{id}/clear. The Ownership Map records exactly two S8 operations, POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, and no GET at all. The FSD needs a synchronous read: AC-EXC-S8-002-02 measures the deviation query against a two second timeout and AC-ALT-S8-007-02 reads agent outputs for a case. The raise path, the clear path and the read path are therefore each named three different ways in three sources, and the read has no recorded owner.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 15 (REST GET/POST /deviations, POST /deviations/{id}/clear) and slide 41 (S8 suffix /deviations). Ownership Map Endpoints: POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, owner S8, no GET. FSD S8 A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-S8-002-02 and A2.7.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-007-02.
proposed: Fix no path in this document beyond the two the Ownership Map records plus the clear operation the Architecture slide records, carry the case-record read as an open question with its owner, and settle all three in the S8 contract story before the screen is built.

title: The Ownership Map gives rwb-deviation one table, while the FSD and the Architecture slide require screening runs, screening scores, contact stops and a breach record as well
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 and slide 41; Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.1.4, A2.7.4, A2.19 and field catalogs
description: The Ownership Map Tables sheet has exactly one row with owner S8, deviation, in schema rwb_deviation, and the platform library objects every service gets. Architecture v5 slide 15 and slide 41 describe the schema as X1-X7 screening, pause, handling and return, and the FSD requires a shadow screening run with a mode, a score row per code with precision, recall and sample size, a contact stop that survives until it is lifted, an agent feedback row and a breach path for a contact sent against a stop. Five of those things have no table, so the DB story cannot be written from the map as it stands.
evidence: Ownership Map Tables: deviation (S8), schema rwb_deviation; no other S8 row. Architecture v5 slide 15 (DB writes schema rwb_deviation: X1-X7 screening, pause, handling, return) and slide 41. FSD S8 A2.1.4.1 AC-S8-001-01 (mode SHADOW, no deviation record), A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-001-01 (one score row per code with precision and recall), A2.7.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-007-01 (agent_feedback verdict ACCEPTED), A2.19 (breach path).
proposed: State the entity groups and their key fields as product requirements, fix no physical table name beyond the one the map already holds, and add the missing rows to the Ownership Map in the same change that writes the S8 DB story.

title: The FSD records an approver on a deviation while the S8 row has no rwb-decision cell and no approval workflow is named for this service
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.2.4.2 and A2.12.3.1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 15 and 25; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Workflows and Endpoints
section: A2.2.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-002-01 (approved in decision log entry DLE-9101 by role U-LG-01); A2.12.3.1 R-DEV-03 and R-DEV-06; A2.12.4 (X3)
description: The case record scenario shows a deviation approved by a second role and cites the decision log entry that approved it, the deceased flow puts Legal beside the specialist, and R-DEV-06 keeps a person as the approver of an insurance claim. The S8 row of the connection matrix has no P7 cell, the S8 workflow list holds DeviationWorkflow alone, and Architecture v5 slide 25 places ApprovalWorkflow on rwb-valuation and rwb-decision only. The FSD's own default model writes the decision record through P7, so the approval and the record are two different questions and only the second one is answered.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.2.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-002-01; A2.12.3.1 R-DEV-03 and R-DEV-06. Architecture v5 slide 13 (S8 row, no P7 cell), slide 15 (TMP DeviationWorkflow only) and slide 25 (ApprovalWorkflow named for rwb-valuation on rwb-decision). Ownership Map Workflows: DeviationWorkflow (S8) and ApprovalWorkflow (P7), no S8 approval entry.
owner_role: Solution architect with the S8 business analyst
proposed: Record the approval the FSD names as a step inside DeviationWorkflow taken by the role the code assigns, with the decision-record library writing the entry and hash, and leave a P7 ApprovalWorkflow to the open question rather than inventing the edge.

title: The FSD calls Aric, NCB, EFS, LIT, SVAF and the partner portal directly while the S8 row has neither an rwb-integration cell nor an outside cell
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.11 to A2.16 integration points; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 15 and 32; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints; Template and Rules DP-16
section: A2.11.2 (EFS); A2.13.2 (Aric); A2.14.2 (LIT); A2.15.2 (NCB, EFS, Partner portal); A2.16.2 (SVAF)
description: Five of the seven X codes reach an outside system: the credit bureau, the fraud system, the external flow system, the litigation system and the appraisal system, plus the partner portal for the skip trace agency. The S8 row of the connection matrix ends at P1, P3 and P10, with no P2 cell and no outside cell, and the Ownership Map records no integration operation for this service. DP-16 makes the integration contract the only carrier of an outside call, so every one of those five paths is blocked until the carrier is named.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.11.2, A2.13.2, A2.14.2, A2.15.2 and A2.16.2 integration points. Architecture v5 slide 13 (S8 row: E to P3, R E to P1, T E to P10, no P2 and no outside cell), slide 15 (OUT: Agent child and Source data party flags only) and slide 32 (Airflow and file transfers at the edges). Ownership Map Endpoints: two S8 operations, no integration operation. Rule DP-16.
owner_role: Solution architect with the integration lead
proposed: Carry each outside effect as a contract dependency on rwb-integration or on the owning service's contract and build against the published fake, with no direct call from this service. Confirm each interface identity (Aric, NCB, EFS, LIT, SVAF) with P2 before the wave 4 test.

title: The screening agent reads call notes and documents, while the S8 row has no rwb-document cell and no call-note data product is named anywhere
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.1.4.1, A2.7.4.2 and A2.10.2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 15 and 33; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints
section: A2.1.4.1 AC-S8-001-01 (200 cases with their call notes and documents); A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-001-02 (DEATH_CERTIFICATE); A2.7.4.2 (complaint note); A2.10.2 (Document hub)
description: Every screening criterion is given a population with its call notes and its documents, and the evidence pack of X1 is assembled from documents. The S8 row of the connection matrix has no P5 cell, the Ownership Map records no document operation for this service, and no source document or contract names the call notes as a data product that a service can read. The input to the flagship agent of this service is therefore unnamed in every source read.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.1.4.1, A2.1.4.2, A2.7.4.2 and A2.10.2. Architecture v5 slide 13 (S8 row, no P5 cell), slide 15 (IN: CaseCreated, AceDataReady, AgentRunCompleted; no document edge) and slide 33 (document intake and text reading are rwb-document and rwb-agent). Ownership Map Endpoints: two S8 operations.
owner_role: Solution architect with the P5 owner
proposed: Carry the document read as a contract dependency on rwb-document and the call-note read as a field of the rwb-source-data contract, and confirm both with their owners before the shadow screening test. No copy of a document is held in schema rwb_deviation.

title: The main success criterion of seven E2 features is the same case-record 'Timers shown' scenario on another story, and every alternate and exception row repeats three scenarios
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.2.4, A2.3.4, A2.4.4, A2.5.4, A2.6.4, A2.8.4 and A2.9.4; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json legacy RWB-E2-015 and RWB-E1-062
description: The main success criterion of the pause, the prescription clock, the routing to the owner, the contact stop, the clear, the low-confidence review and the two-deviation feature is AC-S8-00n-01 'Timers shown', which is the case record view of story RWB-E2-015 and asserts a notice-period timer. The alternate rows are the same deviation-flag and prescription scenarios, and the exception rows are the same four rows in every feature. Nothing in the E2 criterion set proves that a clock pauses, that a stop is set, that a code routes to its owner or that a clear resumes the case, so the evidence of section 11 cannot be stronger than the source.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.2.4.1, A2.3.4.1, A2.4.4.1, A2.5.4.1, A2.6.4.1, A2.8.4.1 and A2.9.4.1 (all 'Timers shown', story RWB-E2-015); A2.2.4.2 to A2.9.4.2 (the same 'Deviation flag' and 'Prescription' rows); A2.2.4.3 to A2.9.4.3 (the same four exception rows). split_plan legacy: RWB-E2-015 is a P3 contract dependency of the S8 story, not an S8-only story.
owner_role: Business analyst, S8 with the QA lead
proposed: Read each criterion row as one criterion, carry it unchanged as the evidence, and add this PRD's own step criterion for the behaviour the row does not assert. The story groomer rewrites the FSD criterion with its owner before the wave 2 test.

title: All ten E7 deviation features carry the placeholder criterion 'Written one epic ahead' and no alternate flow
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.10.4 to A2.19.4; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 8.5
description: The ten features that run X1 to X7 end to end, review an override, match a complaint and open the breach path each have one main success criterion of the form 'The result is recorded with its rule version', with the story column reading 'Written one epic ahead', and 'None. No alternate path' for the alternate flow. The BRD gives each of these features a BR row and a story key, so the capability is specified while its acceptance is not. The PRD can state the requirement and cannot produce an acceptance test from the source.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.10.4.1 AC-S8-010-01 to A2.19.4.1 AC-S8-019-01, all with story cell 'Written one epic ahead'; A2.10.4.2 to A2.19.4.2 ('None. No alternate path'). Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 8.5: BR-062 to BR-069 and RWB-E7-001 to RWB-E7-010.
owner_role: Business analyst, S8 with the QA lead
proposed: Carry the placeholder unchanged in the evidence column, write the wave 4 criteria from the requirement and the rule when the E7 stories are groomed, and keep the placeholder row visible so the gap is not lost.

title: The deceased customer requirement is E3 in the program and the FSD and E7 in the BRD, and the BRD's own question on it is still open
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.15; Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A1.2 and Requirements served; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 8.5, ASM-022 and Q-015
section: A1.2 FEAT-DVF-03 first in E7; Requirements served REQ-DVH-008 epic E3; A2.12
description: The program requirement on death is tagged E3 and the feature that serves it is tagged E7 in the same table, the FSD lists the module as first in 'E2 screening; E7', and the BRD adds an assumption that the deceased flow is read as an E7 deviation flow with the E3 program requirement served through it and leaves Q-015 open for the Product Owner. The service is wave 2, so the question decides whether the X3 slice lands in wave 2, in the E3 release or in wave 4.
evidence: Program v5 section 5.15 (REQ-DVH-008, epic E3) and the service table (RWB-SVC-S8 wave 2, epics EP02, EP03, EP07). FSD S8 A1.2 (FEAT-DVF-03 first in E7) and Requirements served (REQ-DVH-008, E3). Epics 3 to 8 v1 ASM-022 and Q-015.
proposed: Release the X3 contact stop, the heir notification and the insurance claim path as the E3 slice of wave 2, and the full X3 flow with its approver and return point in wave 4. The Product Owner's answer to Q-015 closes the question without moving a date.

title: The FSD names 12 of the 22 R-DEV rules and the deviation rule package is Phase 2 with no owner for S8
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.1.3.1 to A2.19.3.1; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 24 and the packaged-rules gap note; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 deviations route set; Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-062
description: R-DEV-01, 02, 03, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 12, 15, 17 and 18 are named in the feature tables. The design names R-DEV-19 to R-DEV-21 as the re-route, the 10 working day escalation and the unmapped-code route to the team manager, and states that the deviation route set is 22 rules whose package is Phase 2 and still needs an owning service. Ten of the twenty-two rules, and the package itself, therefore have no home in the requirement set of this service.
evidence: FSD S8 the twelve named R-DEV rules. Temporal and Drools Design slide 24 (22 rules, package Phase 2, unmapped code to the team manager by R-DEV-21, escalate after 10 working days by R-DEV-20, resume or re-route by R-DEV-18, R-DEV-19 and EV-07) and the packaged-rules gap note (route sets exist, package codes are Phase 2, each needs one owning service). BR-062 cites R-DEV-01 to R-DEV-22.
owner_role: Center of excellence analyst with P7
proposed: Carry the named rules as the requirement set, name the rule IDs this PRD adds from the design, and leave the package authoring, its version label and its promotion to the rule registry in rwb-decision.

title: The deviation service level is 'set with DL22' and has no number, and the ten working day escalation comes only from the design
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.1.1 to A2.19.1; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 24; Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-003 and DL22
section: A2.1.1, A2.2.1, A2.3.1 and the equivalent intent tables of every feature; A2.5.4.3 and A2.2.4.3
description: Every feature carries the same metric row, 'Deviations closed within the service level', with the target cell reading 'Set with DL22'. The design adds a ten working day escalation and a thirty day skip trace window and cites R-DEV-20 and the X6 clock, while the FSD states neither. No service level, no escalation period and no skip trace window is therefore stated as a value in the requirement set itself.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.1.1 to A2.19.1 metric tables ('Set with DL22'). Temporal and Drools Design slide 8 ('escalates if not resolved in 10 working days') and slide 24 ('Escalate after 10 wd, R-DEV-20'; 'X6 skip trace 30 days'). Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-003 (queue and approval timers, DL22, DL23).
proposed: Carry the service level, the escalation period and the skip trace window as versioned reference data read at run time, assert no number, and take the values from DL22 when the business lead sets them.

title: The confidence threshold for the low-confidence review and the evidence required to run the agent at L1 are not stated
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.7.4 and A2.8; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 24; Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-014 and BR-084
section: A2.7.4.1 AC-S8-007-01 (evaluation on sample SCREEN-S2 version 1, policy P2); A2.7.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-007-01 (one segment, MORTGAGE, BKK); A2.8
description: The L1 feature names the policy, its version, the segment and the evaluation run that justify the level, and the review feature puts a flag below a confidence threshold in front of a person, but no source states the threshold, the measured level that earns L1 on a segment, or who approves the change. The BRD leaves the autonomy evidence question to Q-014 and BR-084 gives the decision to the strategy and model committee.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.7.4.1, A2.7.4.2 and A2.8. Temporal and Drools Design slide 24 ('Low-confidence flags get human review, FEAT-DVH-08'). Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-014 (what measured evidence and threshold justify raising or lowering an autonomy level) and BR-084.
proposed: Read the threshold and the autonomy policy from versioned reference data held by rwb-agent and rwb-decision, assert no number, and leave the evidence pack and the approval of a level change to Q-014 and BR-084.

title: The retention period and the classification scheme of the deviation record are not set
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.8.3.2 and the field catalogs; Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-031 and NFR-047; Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012 and DL26
description: The field catalog marks all eight fields as not personal data and gives no classification, and the FSD states no retention for the deviation record, the screening run or the breach record. NFR-031 requires a retention and archive rule by record class, NFR-047 requires a classification that sets handling, and both are open under DL26 and Q-012. This document therefore assigns a working classification and leaves every period open.
evidence: FSD S8 field catalogs (eight fields, personal data column 'No'). Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-031 (retention by record class, not set), NFR-047 (classification scheme to be applied). Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012 and DL26.
proposed: State the record class and a working classification per entity, state no period, and take the periods and the scheme from DL26 and Q-012 before the first release.

title: The two deviation screens have no owner cell in the Architecture screen matrix and no recorded route at the edge
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 Screens; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Template and Rules DP-19; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints
section: Screens SCR-06 Raise deviation and SCR-08 Deviation queue
description: The FSD gives two screens, the raise screen and the deviation queue, with the queue filtered by type, handler and age. The Ownership Map records no screen and no composite route for them, the service's two endpoints carry no GET that the queue could read, and DP-19 makes every screen a gateway-bff composite route owned at the edge. Neither screen has an owner in the sources read.
evidence: FSD S8 Screens (SCR-06, SCR-08). Architecture v5 slide 41 (the service catalogue). Rule DP-19 (screen becomes a gateway-bff composite route). Ownership Map Endpoints: POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId}, no read.
proposed: Carry both screens as composite routes at the edge over this service's read and command contract, and confirm the read operation and the composite route with the platform edge owner before the wave 2 screen test.

title: The wording, the Thai version and the approver of the eight messages the service shows are not in the FSD
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.1.3.1 to A2.19.3.1; Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-059; Template and Rules DL10
section: MSG-P1-001, MSG-P3-003, MSG-P3-004, MSG-P3-018, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-006
description: Six message IDs appear in the rule tables or the criteria of this module and two more are named by the case record scenarios, and the English wording of only three of them is given in the source. NFR-059 requires every label and message in Thai and in English, and no source names the role that approves either version or holds the wording for S8.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.1.3.1 (MSG-P1-001 wording), A2.8.3.1 (MSG-GEN-001 wording), A2.2.4.2 (MSG-P3-003, MSG-P3-004 by name), A2.2.4.3 (MSG-P3-018, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 by name), A2.2.4.3 (MSG-GEN-006 by name). Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-059. DL10.
proposed: Preserve every message ID and the English wording that exists, serve each message from the message catalogue in Thai and in English, and leave the Thai wording and the approver to DL10.

title: The two deviation events have a catalogue row and a topic but no field list, while the criteria expect an agent verdict and a decision log entry to travel with them
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 43; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Events EV-06 and EV-07; Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.7.4.2
section: A2.7.4.2 AC-ALT-S8-007-01 (agent_feedback holds verdict ACCEPTED with the S8 decision log entry ID); A2.1.4.1 and A2.2.4.2 (contact stop and return point)
description: The event catalogue carries DeviationRaised as EV-06 and DeviationCleared as EV-07 on rwb.deviation.events.v1, owned by this service, with the consumers named. It carries no payload, and the FSD expects an agent verdict, a decision log entry reference, a contact stop flag and a return point to be readable against the deviation. Whether those travel on the event or are read back by the consumer is not stated.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 42 (rows 06 and 07) and slide 43; Ownership Map Events EV-06 and EV-07 (owner S8); FSD S8 A2.7.4.2.
proposed: Carry the two events by name and topic, keyed by the case, with the code, the state, the contact stop flag, the return point and the decision record reference in the envelope, and no personal and no financial value. The schema is written with the contract story.

title: No deviation, screening or queue volume is stated for this module
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 A2.1.4 and A2.7.4; Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-001, NFR-002 and NFR-011; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 33
section: A2.1.4.1 (200 cases in the shadow sample), A2.7.4.1 (500 cases in the evaluation sample); the metric tables
description: The only quantities in the module are the two sample sizes of the agent evaluation, 200 and 500 cases. No source states how many deviations are open at go-live, how many screening runs a night produces, how many items the deviation queue holds or how many rule evaluations the screening needs, so no volume target of this module can be stated and the platform figures are the only ones available.
evidence: FSD S8 A2.1.4.1 and A2.7.4.1. Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-001 (23,600 open cases at go-live, 3,110 new a month), NFR-002 (about 370 staff online of 914) and NFR-011 (300 milliseconds per rule evaluation). Architecture v5 slide 33 (05:00 to 07:00 morning run includes rwb-deviation).
proposed: State the platform population figures and the two evaluation samples, assert no module volume, and measure the real deviation rate in the shadow run before the wave 2 volume test is sized.

title: The change notes of FSD S8 versions 1 and 2 are not in the sources read
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S8 Deviation handling v3 Document control; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6
description: The change note of FSD S8 v3 says what v3 changed and that everything else is unchanged from v2. The v1 and v2 change notes, their dates and their contents are not in the sources read, so the inherited history of this requirement set cannot be reconstructed and is carried as an open item rather than written from memory.
evidence: FSD S8 Document control: 'Change note v3, 15 November 2026 ... Everything else unchanged from v2'. The FSD v6 extract folder holds one file per module, at version 3; no v1 or v2 of S8 is present.
proposed: Carry the version history as 'not specified' in the inherited history table, and let the FSD owner add the v1 and v2 rows when the folder is completed.
